findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, making the final assertion racy
findings.body: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the background thread reading groups is started but never joined. After `deletedAll.set(true)`, the main thread immediately asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty, but the reader thread may still be in the middle of its last `groups(...)` call and can add an exception to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion has passed (a false negative), or the JVM may exit with the thread still running. The test should keep a reference to the Thread, set the flag, call `thread.join()` (with a timeout), and only then assert on `caughtExceptions`.

findings.title: Reader thread spins in a tight loop and can leak if the test fails early
findings.body: The background thread loops `while (!deletedAll.get())` with no sleep and no bound, and `deletedAll` is only set at the end of the happy path. If group creation or deletion throws (e.g. the `fail(...)` in the create loop), the thread runs forever, keeping the test JVM busy hammering the server with `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` requests. Wrapping the delete loop in try/finally to always set the flag (and joining the thread) would make the test robust.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount now silently returns null for a deleted group instead of failing
findings.body: The change converts an NPE into a `null` return when the group has been concurrently deleted (`modelSupplier.get()` returns null). Callers such as `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` then serialize `subGroupCount: null` for a group that no longer exists, masking the deletion rather than surfacing it (every other accessor in this class throws `IllegalStateException("Not found in database")` in that situation). If returning a representation for a deleted group is acceptable this is fine, but the inconsistency is worth a conscious decision — e.g. returning 0 or skipping the group would be clearer contract behavior.
